dedupe_keys.name: commuting analysis of the budapest metropolitan area using mobile network data

description: Gergő Pintér and Imre Felde publish Python notebooks for deriving home, workplace and commuting patterns from mobile-network activity. Zenodo archives version 0.2.0, dated July 2022. Code is MIT-licensed and free; documentation, OpenCellID inputs and OpenStreetMap boundaries retain their separate stated licences. The workflow clusters cells, estimates home and work locations and compares commuting between Budapest districts and surrounding settlements. It can prepare travel-demand assumptions for transport simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers the workflow. Real mobile-network records are withheld because of third-party restrictions. A synthetic generator makes the examples executable, but its spatial activity deliberately does not represent the observed population and must not reproduce the paper’s findings. The study environment lists package versions, not minimum requirements. Data coverage, inference bias and transfer to other cities depend on user-supplied records. No notebooks were executed or private observations requested.
